skill.name: competitor-analysis
skill.description: Analyze competitor websites to compare page structure, messaging, trust signals, features, CTAs, and content gaps for strategy planning.
skill.summary: Research competitor websites and turn page observations into prioritized content and feature recommendations.
skill.author: CleanExpo

content.value_statement: Competitive research can miss page structure, trust signals, and messaging gaps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a repeatable website analysis workflow.
actual_capabilities: Review home, about, services, pricing, contact, and resource pages for structure and messaging.
Capture headlines, supporting copy, CTAs, trust signals, and feature patterns from competitor pages.
Classify competitors as national, regional, local, or emerging for clearer comparison.
Identify missing features, trust signals, messaging themes, and content opportunities.
Produce prioritized recommendations for redesigns, market entry, pricing reviews, or new pages.
limitations: It depends on accessible public web pages and current search results.
It does not verify private analytics, revenue, or traffic data.
It should summarize competitor patterns, not copy protected text or designs.
Website content changes often, so analyses need dates and periodic refreshes.

use_cases.title: Plan a Website Redesign
use_cases.description: Compare competitor pages before changing navigation, offers, CTAs, and credibility sections.

use_cases.title: Enter a New Market
use_cases.description: Map leading and local competitors to find positioning gaps and useful feature ideas.

use_cases.title: Prepare Quarterly Reviews
use_cases.description: Track competitor messaging, content, pricing presentation, and trust signals for recurring strategy updates.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Competitor Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [competitor URL] using the competitor-analysis skill. Focus on homepage structure, core message, CTAs, and trust signals.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Three Competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these competitors: [URLs]. Compare page structures, headline patterns, CTAs, trust signals, unique features, and gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Find Redesign Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [our site] against [competitor URLs]. Identify missing sections, stronger positioning ideas, credibility gaps, and prioritized redesign recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Market Entry Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze national, regional, local, and emerging competitors in [market]. Summarize patterns, gaps, risks, and action priorities for launch planning.

output_examples.output: The report identifies hero message, section order, visible CTAs, trust signals, and unique homepage features. It ends with priority recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare three local competitors before a redesign.
output_examples.output: A comparison highlights common page sections, missing credibility elements, CTA patterns, content gaps, and quick wins for the redesign.
The output summarizes changed messaging, new features, pricing presentation shifts, and recommendations for the next planning cycle.

best_practices: Date every analysis and record source URLs because competitor websites change often.
Separate observed facts from recommendations so teams can review evidence quickly.
Prioritize high-impact gaps instead of listing every difference.
anti_patterns: Copying competitor headlines, layouts, or claims without original positioning work.
Treating a single competitor as proof of market direction.
Using stale screenshots or notes without checking the current website.

faq.question: Does this skill browse competitor websites?
faq.answer: It is designed to guide browser navigation and web search when those tools are available and approved.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports national, regional, local, and emerging competitor comparisons.

faq.question: Will it copy competitor content?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for pattern analysis and explicitly warns against plagiarism.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide competitor URLs, market context, target pages, and the business goal for the analysis.

faq.question: Can it analyze pricing pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews pricing model presentation, conversion points, CTAs, and visible trust signals.

faq.question: How often should analysis be refreshed?
faq.answer: Refresh before redesigns, market launches, pricing changes, and quarterly strategy reviews.
